title: Abdominal Pain Triage Protocol
body: Abdominal pain assessment: Determine location (RUQ, LUQ, RLQ, LLQ, epigastric, periumbilical, diffuse), onset (sudden vs gradual), character (sharp, crampy, colicky, burning), severity (0-10), radiation, and timing (constant vs intermittent). Associated symptoms: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, fever, bloody stool, urinary symptoms. Ask about last menstrual period in females of reproductive age. Red flags: sudden severe pain, rigid abdomen, rebound tenderness described, bloody vomit or stool, fever with severe pain, possible pregnancy with pain.
disposition_notes: Sudden severe pain or rigid abdomen → ER_NOW. Moderate pain with fever or vomiting → URGENT_CARE. Mild cramping without alarm features → SAME_DAY. Chronic mild symptoms → ROUTINE.
